"excerpt": "The must-have ARK mods for 2026 across ASE and ASA, from Structures Plus and Awesome SpyGlass to Dino Storage v2, stacking mods, and map mods like Astraeos.",

"seoDescription": "Top ARK mods for 2026 across ASE and ASA: Structures Plus, Awesome SpyGlass, Dino Storage v2, stacking mods, Classic Flyers, and Astraeos map mods.",
"body": "Modding is what keeps ARK feeling fresh year after year, and 2026 is no exception. Whether you're running the classic **ARK: Survival Evolved (ASE)** or the rebuilt **ARK: Survival Ascended (ASA)**, the right mod list transforms a grindy survival sim into a smooth, quality-of-life-rich server your community will actually stick around on. Here are the best ARK mods for 2026, organized by what they do for your server.

## Quality-of-Life Essentials

No modded ARK server is complete without building and inventory upgrades. **Structures Plus (S+)** — and its community successor **Super Structures** — remains the single most transformative mod you can install. Snap points, pickup timers, auto-crafting stations, and cleaner building make base construction painless. On ASA, S+ features are increasingly baked into the base game, but Super Structures still adds depth veterans expect.

**Awesome SpyGlass!** is another near-mandatory pick. Point it at any dino to instantly read stats, torpor, food, and taming progress. It turns guesswork into information and is beloved on both PvE and PvP servers.

For taming and breeding servers, **Dino Storage v2** is a game-changer. It lets players store creatures as "soul balls," cutting server tame counts dramatically. Fewer active dinos means lower server load and better performance — a win for admins and players alike.

## Movement and Convenience

**Awesome Teleporters!** removes the tedium of crossing huge maps. Set up a teleport network for players, items, and even dinos. Pair it with **Dino Storage v2** and you have a logistics backbone that makes large tribes viable without endless flying.

Speaking of flying, **Classic Flyers** restores the pre-nerf flyer speed and stat scaling that many players sorely miss. It's a staple on servers that want the old-school ARK feel where a leveled Argentavis could actually outrun trouble.

## Stacking and Rates

**Stacking mods** are essential for reducing inventory clutter and vault sprawl. Popular options increase stack sizes for resources and consumables, meaning fewer trips and less lag from thousands of item entities. Combined with sensible harvest and taming rates in your server config, stacking mods define the pace of your server.

## Map Mods and New Worlds

One of the biggest draws of 2026 is the wave of high-quality custom maps. **Astraeos** has become a standout — a sprawling, beautifully crafted map with fresh biomes, points of interest, and boss arenas that give veteran players somewhere new to explore. Custom maps like Astraeos are among the most popular reasons players seek out modded servers, so featuring one is a great way to stand out.

## ASE vs. ASA: Where Mods Come From

Here's the crucial difference for 2026. **ASE uses the Steam Workshop** for mods — you subscribe to items and reference them by their Workshop IDs. **ASA uses CurseForge** instead, with mods identified by CurseForge project IDs and delivered through the game's built-in mod system. Many popular mod names (S+, Dino Storage, Awesome SpyGlass) exist on both platforms, but they are separate uploads. Always confirm you're grabbing the correct version for your game, and check that every mod on your list is compatible with your current game build before launch.

## Building a Balanced Mod List

A great mod list is curated, not maxed out. Start with the essentials — a structures mod, SpyGlass, a stacking mod, and Dino Storage — then layer in flavor like Classic Flyers or a custom map. Test load order and watch for conflicts, especially between multiple structures or stacking mods. Fewer, well-chosen mods almost always beat a bloated list that stutters and crashes.

## Run It on Nxeon

Managing a modded ARK server shouldn't require wrestling with config files. Nxeon's [ARK server hosting](/ark-server-hosting) includes a **one-click Mods manager** that handles both Steam Workshop (ASE) and CurseForge (ASA) mods for you — add, remove, and reorder mods from a clean dashboard, and let your clients auto-download everything on join. Spin up a server, drop in the mods above, and your community can be exploring Astraeos within minutes.

Ready to build your dream ARK server? Pick your map, load your mods, and let Nxeon handle the rest."

"title": "How to Install ARK Mods on Your Server",
"excerpt": "A step-by-step guide to installing ARK mods on your server, covering Steam Workshop IDs for ASE, CurseForge IDs for ASA, the ActiveMods and -mods= launch args, and client auto-download.",
"category": "Gaming",

"seoDescription": "Install ARK mods step by step: Steam Workshop IDs (ASE) vs CurseForge IDs (ASA), the ActiveMods and -mods launch args, load order, and client auto-download.",
"body": "Installing mods on an ARK server is straightforward once you understand how ARK loads them — and the process differs between **ARK: Survival Evolved (ASE)** and **ARK: Survival Ascended (ASA)**. This guide walks through both, plus the launch arguments and load-order tips that keep a modded server stable.

## Step 1: Find Your Mod IDs

Every ARK mod is referenced by an ID, and where you get that ID depends on your game.

**For ASE**, mods live on the **Steam Workshop**. Open a mod's Workshop page and the ID is the long number at the end of the URL (for example, `?id=731604991`). That number is what your server needs.

**For ASA**, mods live on **CurseForge**. Each mod has a CurseForge project ID shown on its page and used by ASA's built-in mod system. ASA downloads mods automatically through this system, so you generally don't hand-place files the way you might have with older ASE setups.

Collect the IDs for every mod you want, in the order you intend to load them.

## Step 2: Tell the Server Which Mods to Load

ARK reads its active mods in one of two ways.

The most common method is the **ActiveMods** line in your `GameUserSettings.ini`, under the `[ServerSettings]` section. List your mod IDs separated by commas, with no spaces:

`ActiveMods=731604991,111111111,222222222`

Alternatively, you can pass mods on the command line using the **`-mods=` launch argument**:

`-mods=731604991,111111111,222222222`

Both achieve the same result — pick one method and stick with it to avoid confusion. If you set both, the launch argument typically wins, so don't split your list across the two.

## Step 3: Mind the Load Order

The **order of your mod IDs matters**. ARK loads mods top to bottom, and later mods can override earlier ones. As a rule of thumb, load total-conversion and map mods appropriately for their type, and place mods that modify the same systems (like multiple structures or stacking mods) carefully so the one you want to "win" loads last. If something behaves unexpectedly after adding a mod, reordering your list is the first thing to try.

## Step 4: Map Mods Are a Special Case

If you're running a custom map like Astraeos, you don't just add it to your mod list — you also set the map name in your server's startup so ARK loads that world instead of the default. The map mod still needs to be in your active mods so it downloads, but the server's map/level parameter is what actually points ARK at it. Check the map mod's page for the exact map name to use.

## Step 5: Clients Auto-Download Everything

Here's the good news for your players: **clients automatically download mods when they join**. When someone connects to your modded server, ARK pulls the required Workshop items (ASE) or CurseForge mods (ASA) in the background before they spawn in. You don't need to send players a manual mod pack or installation instructions — as long as your server's mod list is correct, joining does the rest. Just make sure your players are on the same game build and the mods are up to date, since version mismatches are the most common cause of "failed to load" errors.

## Troubleshooting Common Issues

If mods won't load, check the basics first: confirm every ID is correct, ensure there are no spaces in your comma-separated list, and verify each mod supports your current game version. A single outdated or delisted mod can prevent the whole server from starting. Restart the server after any mod change so it re-downloads and re-reads the list cleanly.

## The Easy Way with Nxeon

Editing INI files and juggling launch arguments is doable, but it's easy to fat-finger an ID. Nxeon's [ARK server hosting](/ark-server-hosting) includes a **one-click Mods manager** that lets you add mods by ID, reorder your load order with drag-and-drop, and switch maps without touching a config file. It works for both ASE Workshop mods and ASA CurseForge mods, validates your list before launch, and restarts cleanly so clients auto-download on join. Set your mods once and get back to playing."

"body": "Palworld exploded onto the scene as one of the biggest survival-crafting hits in recent memory, and by 2026 its dedicated-server community is thriving. While the modding ecosystem is still young compared to veterans like ARK or Conan, the tools are maturing fast — and Palworld's rich **server settings** already give admins enormous control over how their world plays. This guide covers both: the settings worth tuning and the mods worth watching.

## Start With Server Settings

Before you even think about mods, Palworld's built-in configuration (via `PalWorldSettings.ini`) is where most servers get their personality. These are the most-tuned settings for 2026.

**Rate multipliers** are the heart of any server's feel. Key ones include `ExpRate` (leveling speed), `PalCaptureRate` (how easily you catch Pals), `PalSpawnNumRate` (how many Pals roam the world), and the collection/gathering rates for items and eggs. Boosting capture and EXP rates creates a faster, more casual server; dialing them down makes progression a real grind for hardcore groups.

**Day and night length** (`DayTimeSpeedRate`, `NightTimeSpeedRate`) changes the survival rhythm. Longer nights raise the stakes; longer days ease resource runs.

**Pal and player condition rates** — hunger depletion, HP, damage dealt and taken — let you tune difficulty precisely. Many servers soften hunger and stamina drain for a smoother co-op experience while keeping combat damage punchy.

## PvP and Base Settings
